$comment: ENH-005: hand-authored vault-resolution vectors shared by Python (tests/test_vault_resolver_parity.py) and TypeScript (visualizer/lib/vaultResolver.parity.test.ts). Validated structurally by scripts/gen_parity_fixtures.py. {TMP} is substituted to a per-test temp directory by both harnesses, and both sides resolve() paths before comparing so macOS /private prefixing is handled. applies_to scopes a vector to one language when the resolver contract genuinely differs (documented below); every vector is executed or explicitly excluded by both suites -- no silent skips. SEC-P001: the Python resolver is now allowlist-based (named vaults from vaults.yaml + the default vault); arbitrary paths from .claude/vault / CLAUDE_VAULT fall through to the default instead of being accepted.

fields.explicit: Argument passed to the resolver (Python: explicit= kwarg; TS: vaultName arg). null/omit = call with no argument.
fields.cwd: Working directory (Python only; TS has no cwd concept). Defaults to {TMP} on the Python side.
fields.cwd_marker: Path of a .claude/vault file to write (Python branch 2). cwd_marker_content supplies its body.
fields.env_CLAUDE_VAULT: Python branch 3 env var. null = unset. TS does not read this var.
fields.env_VAULT_ROOT: TS getDefaultVault() override. null = unset. Python resolve_vault() does not read this var.
fields.vaults_yaml: Body written to $HOME/.config/parsidion/vaults.yaml before the call.
fields.mkdir: Directories to create before the call.
fields.expect: Expected resolved vault path ({TMP}-substituted). Mutually exclusive with expect_error.
fields.expect_error: If present (a label string), expect a VaultConfigError. The label documents the reason; both suites assert the error class, not the label text.

vectors.name: default-vault-no-overrides
vectors.description: With no explicit/cwd-marker/env overrides, both resolvers return $HOME/ParsidionVault.

vectors.name: default-vault-legacy-fallback
vectors.description: When ~/ClaudeVault exists and ~/ParsidionVault does not, the default flips to the legacy name.

vectors.name: named-vault-from-yaml
vectors.description: A vault registered in vaults.yaml resolves by name on both sides.

vectors.name: unknown-name-rejected
vectors.description: A name not in vaults.yaml (and not the default) is rejected by both sides.

vectors.name: default-path-passed-explicitly
vectors.description: The default vault's own path resolves whether passed by name or path. Both resolvers match it against the default vault path.

vectors.name: named-vault-forbidden-rejected
vectors.description: A named vault registered to a forbidden system path (/etc) is rejected by both sides -- Python validates in _resolve_vault_reference, TS validates after the named lookup.

vectors.name: forbidden-path-explicit-rejected
vectors.description: Explicit /etc: Python rejects (not in allowlist); TS rejects (not allowlisted). Both raise VaultConfigError -- the suites assert the class, not the reason.

vectors.name: arbitrary-path-rejected
vectors.description: SEC-P001: an arbitrary path that is neither a named vault nor the default vault is rejected by BOTH resolvers. Previously Python accepted it (documented divergence); SEC-P001 closed the gap by back-porting the TS allowlist.

vectors.name: explicit-overrides-claude-vault-python
vectors.description: Python branch 1 (explicit) beats branch 3 (CLAUDE_VAULT). Both vault paths are registered in vaults.yaml so the allowlist resolver accepts them.

vectors.name: explicit-overrides-cwd-marker-python
vectors.description: Python branch 1 (explicit) beats branch 2 (cwd/.claude/vault). Both paths registered in vaults.yaml for the allowlist.

vectors.name: cwd-marker-overrides-claude-vault-python
vectors.description: Python branch 2 (cwd/.claude/vault) beats branch 3 (CLAUDE_VAULT). Both paths registered in vaults.yaml so the allowlist resolver accepts the .claude/vault reference.

vectors.name: claude-vault-overrides-default-python
vectors.description: Python branch 3 (CLAUDE_VAULT) beats branch 4 (default). env-vault registered in vaults.yaml for the allowlist.

vectors.name: cwd-marker-empty-falls-through-python
vectors.description: An empty/whitespace .claude/vault file is skipped -- falls through to CLAUDE_VAULT. env-vault registered for the allowlist.

vectors.name: cwd-marker-missing-falls-through-python
vectors.description: A cwd with no .claude/vault file falls through to CLAUDE_VAULT. env-vault registered for the allowlist.

vectors.name: cwd-marker-arbitrary-falls-through-python
vectors.description: SEC-P001 exploit mitigation: a .claude/vault pointing at an arbitrary path NOT registered in vaults.yaml is silently skipped -- the resolver falls through to the default vault rather than writing vault content into the attacker-chosen location. No CLAUDE_VAULT is set, so the final result is the default.

vectors.name: claude-vault-arbitrary-falls-through-python
vectors.description: SEC-P001: CLAUDE_VAULT pointing at an arbitrary path not in vaults.yaml falls through to the default vault (graceful degradation, no crash).

vectors.name: claude-vault-forbidden-falls-through-python
vectors.description: SEC-P001: CLAUDE_VAULT pointing at a forbidden system path (/etc) is rejected by the allowlist and falls through to the default vault. Previously this raised VaultConfigError; now the resolver degrades gracefully.

vectors.name: vault-root-overrides-default-typescript
vectors.description: TS getDefaultVault() honors $VAULT_ROOT. Python resolve_vault() does not read VAULT_ROOT -- it uses CLAUDE_VAULT for env override (see claude-vault-overrides-default-python). This is a documented design split, not drift: the visualizer is a server with its own default-override var.

vectors.name: vault-root-forbidden-rejected-typescript
vectors.description: VAULT_ROOT pointing at a forbidden system path is rejected by validateVaultPath.
